jobs.occupation: Full Stack Engineer, Risk Management
jobs.description:
At NORDEN, we empower global trade through data, technology and deep industry knowledge. Behind every decision, there is a need to understand risk, navigate uncertainty and create transparency.

This is where you will contribute. You will build solutions that are used by risk management and commercial teams to manage their trading books and finance to consolidate the business into the value of NORDEN.

Why this role?

You will work across the full development lifecycle, from architecture to implementing solutions and ensuring stable operations in production. At the same time, you will gain unique insights into risk management in a global shipping company.

Our solutions are built in Python with Azure as cloud platform. We use GitHub Copilot with access to the latest models while insisting on having a firm understanding of our code.

You will join a friendly, collaborative and people-focused environment where your ideas are welcomed, your development is supported and your contributions genuinely matter. You will join an experienced team of seven people with backgrounds in computer science, physics and economics.

What you will be doing

As a full-stack engineer, you will play an important role in developing solutions that support key business decisions across NORDEN.

Among other things, you will:

• Build end-to-end scalable and maintainable solutions based on best practice.

• Develop backend services in Python on Azure, using technologies such as Polars, Durable functions and Delta Lake.

• Develop interactive web frontends in React and TypeScript on Azure App Service.

• Get a business-oriented mindset and a genuine interest in shipping and risk management.

• Work on solutions with data scientists, risk managers and finance business partners.

What you bring

We are looking for an experienced engineer who can contribute from day one and is interested in learning about shipping and risk management.

You have:

• A genuine passion for software development and a proven experience within both frontend and backend development.

• Good experience with development in Python and utilising Azure cloud technologies.

• Up to 5 years of experience from a similar position in shipping or the financial sector with a background in computer science, software engineering or similar.

• Interest in exploring new topics on your own, and work well with others when making and explaining decisions.

• Advanced English communication skills

• The legal right to work in Denmark.

Beyond your technical skills, you enjoy collaborating with others and are comfortable engaging with a variety of stakeholders across the organisation. You are curious by nature, open to new ideas and motivated by continuously improving how things are done.

If you are interested in bringing together software development, business insight and modern cloud technologies at a global company where your work makes a clear difference, we would like to hear from you.

Application

Please upload your motivation letter, resume and relevant diplomas via our website as soon as possible and no later than 3 December 2026. Your motivation letter helps us understand what drives you, why you are interested in the role, and how your skills and experiences could contribute to the team. We are especially interested in your motivation and transferable skills, not a recap of your CV. It is your opportunity to tell us the story behind your application.

We review and interview candidates on an ongoing basis.

We will do our best to get back to you at least within ten working days after the application deadline, 3 December 2026.

In NORDEN we value a range of perspectives, educational backgrounds and professional experience and encourages all qualified candidates to apply.

Our company

We are a global provider of ocean-based freight services for bulk and project cargo of all sizes. We integrate freight solutions with port logistics, helping our customers optimise and decarbonise supply chains. We provide tailored solutions built on flexibility, reliability, and intelligence.

Our agile business model ensures stability by continuously adapting our fleet to market developments and customer needs.

Founded in 1871, NORDEN is one of Denmark’s oldest internationally operating shipping companies. Incorporated in Denmark, we are listed on Nasdaq Copenhagen as part of the OMX Nordic Large Cap index.

With offices across 6 continents, we are a truly integrated part of global trade.

jobs.description:
Imagine a future where you shape our view of European power markets and turn deep market insight into commercial action

Application deadline 30th November 2026 , 23:59 CET

Country Denmark

Location Gentofte

Workplace Hybrid (office and home-working) We offer a workplace culture where you´ll arrange with your people leader when you can work from home and from the office.

Working hours full-time

Why join?

Proven very high employee satisfaction and motivation

Continuous development opportunities for all employees

Competitive salary, pension scheme, and attractive holiday package

A wide range of health benefits, such as health insurance, nutritious food, and fitness facilities in our office locations

Join us in this role where you’ll own and continuously develop our fundamental view of European power markets. Working at the intersection of market analysis and trading, you’ll bring together insights from across the organisation, form an independent view of where markets are heading, and translate this into clear commercial recommendations.

Working closely with the Trading & Revenue senior leadership, trading desk heads, and traders, you’ll influence decisions around trading strategies, hedging, portfolio management, and PPAs. Rather than supporting decisions from a distance, you’ll be a trusted market expert whose analysis and judgement help shape the positions we take.

**Welcome to Trading & Revenue

**You’ll be part of Forecasting & Analysis where you, together with your colleagues, will provide the market insights and analysis behind key trading and commercial decisions. You’ll work in a dynamic environment close to the trade floor, collaborating with traders, analysts, meteorologists, and dedicated in-house model developers. With strong modelling capabilities around you, you’ll be able to focus on interpreting what is happening in the market, challenging existing assumptions, forming a strong fundamental view, and translating it into commercial opportunities.

As a team, we challenge our thinking, share our expertise openly, and combine different perspectives to make better decisions.

In this role, your analysis becomes action. You’ll engage directly with Trading & Revenue senior leadership team and have the opportunity to shape how we understand European power markets. You’ll play a leading role in strengthening our market analysis capability, bringing in external perspectives and best practices, and developing a more integrated view across Trading & Revenue.

You’ll play an important role in:

• owning, developing, and maintaining our fundamental view of European power markets, with a particular focus on North-Western Europe and the UK, and bringing together perspectives from across Trading & Revenue into a coherent market outlook

• acting as a trusted sparring partner to the Trading & Revenue senior leadership, trading desk heads, traders, and portfolio managers, bringing an independent fundamental market perspective to key strategic and commercial decisions

• identifying structural and emerging shifts across supply, demand, regulation, weather, generation, interconnector flows, electrification, and other market drivers, and assessing what they mean for power prices and market dynamics

• turning market developments into commercial implications, from understanding the impact of changing generation availability or demand assumptions to assessing what these developments mean for our portfolios and trading positions

• translating fundamental market insights into actionable trading and hedging strategies together with our trading teams, helping facilitate discussions on what positions we should take as market conditions and assumptions evolve

• advising senior stakeholders on the market implications of important portfolio, PPA, and other commercial decisions, bringing a clear view of both market opportunities and risks

• advancing our fundamental power market capability by bringing together perspectives from across the organisation, introducing external insights and industry best practices, and strengthening how we form and communicate our market view across Trading & Revenue.

To succeed in the role, you:

• have deep expertise in European power markets and significant experience forming an independent view of how fundamental developments affect power prices and market dynamics

• bring strong commercial judgement and can move confidently from fundamental analysis to clear recommendations on trading, hedging, portfolio, and PPA decisions

• understand the interaction between physical power market fundamentals, forward markets, options, and curve dynamics, and can connect changes in the physical market with their commercial and trading implications

• are comfortable owning a market view, challenging established assumptions, and acting as an equal sparring partner to experienced traders and senior decision-makers

• can look beyond established market assumptions, identify developments or structural shifts that may not yet be fully reflected in the market view, and determine what they could mean for future power prices

• can bring together different sources of analysis, modelling, external intelligence, and perspectives from across the organisation to form a clear and coherent market view

• communicate complex market developments as concise, decisive, and commercially relevant recommendations, including to senior stakeholders

• bring substantial experience from power or closely related European energy markets, whether gained in a utility, trading environment, financial institution, or similar market-facing organization.

Maybe you’ve read the above and can see you have some transferable skills, even though they don’t quite match all the points. If you think you can bring something to the team, we still encourage you to apply.

Actual pay will be based on skills, experience, and the expected role fulfilment to ensure a fair and competitive offer. Where applicable, you may also be eligible for variable payment and a comprehensive benefits package. Pay details specific to your location will be provided during the interview process.

Pre-employment background checks:

For certain positions, a background check may be required as part of the hiring process. Because we recruit across multiple countries, the specific checks performed will depend on the role and the legal requirements in the location where the position is filled. If a background check is relevant for the role you are being considered for, you will be informed during the recruitment process. All background checks are carried out by an external provider and always in accordance with applicable local laws and regulations.

Shape the technical direction and build software that lasts

At Autorola, we're transforming the global automotive industry through digital solutions, technology and business intelligence.

We're looking for an experienced Staff Software Engineer to take technical ownership of a team's domain, guide architectural decisions and ensure high engineering quality across our software solutions.

You'll combine hands-on software development with technical leadership, working closely with Product Managers, engineers and other technical specialists to turn business needs into robust, scalable and maintainable solutions.

If you're passionate about software architecture, solving complex technical challenges and helping other engineers grow, we'd love to hear from you.

About us

The Autorola Group is a global leader in online vehicle remarketing, automotive IT solutions and business intelligence for the used vehicle market.

Through Autorola Marketplace, Autorola Solutions and Indicata, we help manufacturers, leasing companies, fleet owners and dealers buy, sell and manage vehicles more efficiently using technology, data and digital solutions.

Your role

As Staff Software Engineer, you'll be the team's technical anchor and go-to person, taking ownership of its technical direction, architecture and engineering standards.

You'll remain hands-on in software development while leading technical design discussions, making architectural decisions and guiding the team towards solutions that support both immediate business needs and long-term technical sustainability.

You'll work closely with the Team Lead, Product Manager, Principal Engineers and other department-level technical roles to align team decisions with Autorola's wider technology strategy.

Success means a well-architected and maintainable technical domain, high engineering standards, effective collaboration and a team that continues to grow technically.

What you'll be doing

• Take architectural ownership of the team's technical domain, including services, data models, interfaces, dependencies and technical documentation.

• Guide technical direction and ensure alignment with Autorola's architecture principles, engineering standards and technology strategy.

• Stay hands-on in software development, designing, building, testing and delivering high-quality solutions.

• Lead technical design discussions, reviews and decisions, making trade-offs between business needs, delivery speed and long-term maintainability.

• Drive modernisation initiatives, including breaking down legacy applications, improving system architecture and reducing duplication across teams.

• Collaborate with Principal Engineers and other Staff Engineers to align team architecture with company-wide strategies.

• Mentor and coach engineers, support technical problem-solving and help raise the overall engineering capabilities of the team.

• Promote best practices in automated testing, CI/CD, code reviews and responsible use of AI-assisted development tools.

Who are we looking for

We're looking for a senior software engineer with deep technical expertise, strong architectural understanding and the ability to guide others through complex technical decisions. You are likely to have:

• A bachelor's or master's degree in computer science, software engineering or similar, or equivalent practical experience.

• Typically, 8+ years of professional software development experience, including ownership of system architecture or a technical domain.

• Proven experience designing, building and operating production systems, including architecture, performance, security and monitoring.

• Experience modernising legacy applications and designing scalable, maintainable software architectures.

• Experience with cloud technologies, preferably AWS, and event-driven architecture.

• Strong knowledge of automated testing, CI/CD and code review practices.

• The ability to lead technical initiatives, make sound architectural decisions and communicate complex topics clearly to different stakeholders.

• Experience mentoring and coaching other engineers.

• Experience with technologies such as Java, Spring Boot, REST APIs, relational databases and AWS is relevant.

What success looks like

Within your first 12–18 months, you'll have:

• Established clear technical ownership of your team's domain, including architecture, services, dependencies and documentation.

• Built strong relationships with Product Management, Team Leads, Principal Engineers and other technical stakeholders.

• Guided the team towards consistent engineering standards and sustainable architectural decisions.

• Delivered visible progress on modernisation and reduced technical debt within your domain.

• Improved software quality, maintainability, scalability and operational reliability.

• Helped raise the technical capabilities of the team through mentoring, knowledge sharing and technical leadership.

• Contributed to aligning your team's technical direction with Autorola's wider technology strategy.

Why join Autorola Group?

Autorola Group is a global company with more than 850 employees across 20 subsidiaries in Europe, Latin America and Asia-Pacific.

You'll join an international technology environment where software engineering, business expertise and digital solutions come together to solve complex challenges for leading automotive companies.

As Staff Software Engineer, you'll have a significant influence on our technical direction, architectural decisions and engineering standards. You'll work alongside skilled engineers and technical specialists, with the opportunity to shape solutions, drive modernisation and help build the next generation of Autorola's technology platforms.

We also offer pension and health insurance, social and company events, a great lunch arrangement, access to a fitness room and a lively Friday bar.

Want to join the team?

We strongly believe in inclusion and diversity and encourage you to apply even if you don't meet every requirement. Applications and CVs will be reviewed on an ongoing basis, and the advertisement may be removed once the right candidate has been found.

If you have any questions about the position, feel free to contact Christian Gless, Tech Talent Acquisition Partner, on csg@autorola.com.

jobs.occupation: Up to 3 PhD fellowships in Quantum error correction
jobs.description:
The Quantum error correction team at the Novo Nordisk Foundation Quantum Computing Programme (NQCP) invites applicants for up to three PhD fellowships.

  The start date is (expected to be) 1 April, 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  The programme
 The Novo Nordisk Foundation Quantum Computing Program (NQCP), funded by the Novo Nordisk Foundation, is building a talented and diverse international team to create a cutting-edge program in the heart of Copenhagen, Denmark. At the Niels Bohr Institute, University of Copenhagen, where the formulation of Quantum Mechanics was born 100 years ago, the ambition is to build a mission-driven full-stack approach which will involve exciting innovations at every level, from the quantum processor to the quantum-classical interface, all the way to quantum algorithms and applications. The vision of the programme is to enable the development of fault-tolerant quantum computing hardware and quantum algorithms that solve important problems in the life sciences.

  The project
 Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires low logical error rates together with resource-efficient, experimentally feasible approaches to quantum error correction. Our research spans low-overhead quantum error-correcting codes, efficient syndrome extraction, high-fidelity parity measurements, and scalable hardware architectures. We aim to connect these efforts with fault-tolerant logical operations, taking into account the noise characteristics, connectivity, and operational constraints of quantum computing platforms. In our work, we are collaborating closely with all of the different teams at NQCP; see nqcp.ku.dk.

  We are looking for up to three motivated PhD candidates to undertake research within theoretical effort for quantum error-correction. We are interested in developing a project plan with prospective candidates to best match their skills and experience to the activities in the QEC team. We imagine that the candidates would undertake research within one or more of the following topics:

   	
• Investigation of low-overhead and high-threshold error-correctable codes, including low-density parity check codes 	
• Resource estimation and optimization for scalable quantum computing over different hardware platforms 	
• Distributed quantum error correction on modular design and quantum networks 	
• Optimization of syndrome extraction circuits, error correction cycle, and fault-tolerant logical operation   Who are we looking for?
 We are looking for candidates within the field(s) of Physics, Computational Physics, Quantum Information, or a closely related field, with a focus on theoretical and/or computational quantum physics.

  Successful candidates will have:

   	
• Strong analytical and computational skills 	
• Strong knowledge of quantum mechanics and quantum information 	
• An interest in developing quantum error correction methods that account for hardware capabilities and limitations 	
• A passion for developing theoretical protocols 	
• Ability to work both independently and collaboratively in a dynamic research environment 	
• Knowledge of quantum error correction or quantum computing platforms, including photonic systems and superconducting circuits, is an advantage.   Our group and research - and what do we offer?
 We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in a dynamic and international research environment hosted by the NNF Quantum Computing Programme (NQCP) at the Niels Bohr Institute, University of Copenhagen.

  The project will be supervised by Assistant Professor Maryam Khanahmadi, maryam.khanahmadi@nbi.ku.dk, QEC team lead, and the principal supervisor will be Stefano Paesani, stefano.paesani@nbi.ku.dk.

  Qualifications needed 
 To be eligible for the regular PhD programme, you must have completed a degree programme, equivalent to a Danish master’s degree (180 ECTS/3 FTE BSc + 120 ECTS/2 FTE MSc) related to the subject area of the project, e.g. a degree in Physics, Applied Physics, Photonics, Quantum Information or similar. For information on eligibility of completed programmes, see General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.

  Terms of employment 
 Employment as a PhD fellow is full-time and for a maximum of 3 years.

  Employment is conditional upon your successful enrolment as a PhD student at the PhD School at the Faculty of SCIENCE, University of Copenhagen. This requires submission and acceptance of an application for the specific project formulated by the applicant.

  Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

  Appointment will be subject to receipt of a security clearance.

  You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

  Responsibilities and tasks in the PhD programme

   	
• Carry through an independent research project under supervision 	
• Complete PhD courses corresponding to approx. 30 ECTS / ½ FTE 	
• Participate in active research environments, including a stay at another research institution, preferably abroad 	
• Teaching and knowledge dissemination activities 	
• Write scientific papers aimed at high-impact journals 	
• Write and defend a PhD thesis on the basis of your project   We are looking for the following qualifications:

   	
• Professional qualifications relevant to the PhD project 	
• Relevant publications 	
• Relevant work experience 	
• Good language and communication skills 	
• Willingness to work in a team 	
• Willingness to engage actively with the other teams at NQCP    Application and Assessment Procedure
 Your application including all attachments must be in English and submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.

  Please include: 

   	
• Motivated letter of application (max. one page) 	
• Please note that there is the possibility of including an educational part to the PhD project. Therefore, please indicate in the application whether you would be interested in this.  	
• Curriculum vitae including information about your education, experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position 	
• Original degree diplomas and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorized English translation if issued in another language than English or Danish. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted. 	
• Publication list (if possible) 	
• Reference letters (if available)   Application deadline
 The deadline for applications is 6 December 2026, 23:59 GMT +1. 

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

  The further process 
 After the deadline, a number of applicants will be selected for academic assessment by an unbiased expert assessor. You will be notified whether you will be passed for assessment.

  The assessor will assess the qualifications and experience of the shortlisted applicants with respect to the above mentioned research area, techniques, skills and other requirements. The assessor will conclude whether each applicant is qualified and, if so, for which of the two models. The assessed applicants will have the opportunity to comment on their assessment. You can read about the recruitment process here.

  Questions
 For specific information about the PhD fellowship, please contact Maryam Khanahmadi: maryam.khanahmadi@nbi.ku.dk

  General information about PhD study at the Faculty of SCIENCE is available at the PhD School’s website.

   

  The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the surrounding community and invites all regardless of personal background to apply for the position.

jobs.occupation: PhD in Quantum Control Theory for Quantum Algorithms
jobs.description:
The Department of Electronic Systems at The Technical Faculty of IT and Design invites applications for a 3-year PhD stipend in the field of quantum control theory for quantum algorithms within the general study programme Electronical and Electronic Engineering, as per January 1st 2027, or soon hereafter.

In electronic engineering, Aalborg University is known worldwide for its high academic quality and societal impact. The Department of Electronic Systems employs more than 200 people, of which about 90 are PhD students, and about 40 % of all employees are internationals. In total, it has more than 600 students in its BSc and MSc programs, which are based on AAU's problem-based learning model. The department leverages its unique research infrastructure and lab facilities to conduct world-leading fundamental and applied research within communication, networks, control systems, AI, sound, cyber security, and robotics. The department plays an active role in transferring inventions and results into applications in close collaboration with industrial partners worldwide. You can read more about the department at www.es.aau.dk.

Your work tasks

The position is part of the research project QUANTA – Quantum Control Theory for Quantum Algorithms, funded by the Independent Research Fund Denmark. Real quantum computers are open quantum systems: noise and decoherence act on the computation while it runs, so the idealised picture of a sequence of perfect unitary gates acting on an isolated system does not hold in practice. QUANTA therefore regards a quantum program as an open dynamical system, described by Kraus operators in discrete time and by the controlled Lindblad master equation in continuous time, and treats the choice of quantum gates as control decisions. The aim is to use control theory to design quantum algorithms, in particular optimisation algorithms, that are robust to noise and disturbances.

As a PhD student you will work mainly on two parts of the project. The first concerns reach-avoidance for quantum systems: computing the probability that a quantum process reaches a target set of states before it enters a set of forbidden states, and designing control strategies, for example by dynamic programming, that steer the computation towards its goal while respecting such constraints. You will develop this theory for quantum Markov chains described by Kraus operators and for continuous-time systems described by the Lindblad master equation.

The second part applies these results to quantum optimisation. You will develop algorithms in which an optimisation problem, starting with semidefinite programming and continuing with bilinear and polynomial problems, is solved by a quantum system regarded as a control system, including constrained problems formulated as reach-avoidance. You will analyse how the resulting quantum circuits scale with the problem size and test the algorithms on a real quantum computer.

You will work closely with the principal investigator, a postdoctoral researcher on the project and the project's international collaborators, and the project includes research stays at partner institutions abroad. You will present your results at international conferences and in scientific journals, and they will form the basis of your PhD thesis. As part of the PhD programme you will follow PhD courses and take part in teaching and supervision of student projects at the department.

Your competencies You hold a Master's degree in control engineering, electrical engineering, applied mathematics, physics, computer science or a related field. We are looking for a candidate with a solid mathematical background, for example in linear algebra, dynamical systems, control theory, optimisation or probability theory, and with a genuine interest in quantum computing.

Knowledge of quantum mechanics or quantum information is an advantage, but not a requirement – what matters is that you are motivated to learn it during the project. Programming experience, for example in Python, is also an advantage. We value curiosity, the ability to work independently and the willingness to share ideas and help colleagues. You communicate well in English, both orally and in writing.

Qualification requirements

PhD stipends are allocated to individuals who hold a Master's degree. PhD stipends are normally for a period of 3 years. It is a prerequisite for allocation of the stipend that the candidate will be enrolled as a PhD student at the Technical Doctoral School of IT and Design in accordance with the regulations of Ministerial Order No. 872 of 6 October 2026 on the PhD Programme at the Universities and Certain Higher Artistic Educational Institutions. According to the Ministerial Order, the progress of the PhD student shall be assessed at regular points in time. As part of the PhD study, you are among other things required to complete PhD courses corresponding to 30 ECTS, gain experience with teaching or other forms of knowledge dissemination and complete an external research stay outside of Aalborg University, preferably 3-6 months at a foreign research institution.

Who we are

The position is hosted by the Learning and Decisions Lab at the Department of Electronic Systems, Aalborg University, led by Professor Rafal Wisniewski. The lab develops theory and algorithms at the intersection of control theory, stochastic systems, optimisation and quantum computing, including stability and safety of stochastic and quantum systems and feedback control of quantum hardware. You will join a team of senior researchers, PhD students and postdoctoral fellows working on related problems, in an informal and international environment with weekly meetings and close day-to-day supervision

Expected start date and duration of employment

This is a two-year position from 1 February 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.

Job description

We are seeking a motivated postdoc to work on two closely linked research activities throughout the position.

Nitrous oxide (N2O) emissions from nitrogen that leaches from agricultural fields to streams, lakes and other water bodies are estimated to make up around 5% of the Danish agricultural sector’s greenhouse gas emissions, but this estimate is highly uncertain. The Aqua-N2O project, funded by the Independent Research Fund Denmark (DFF), aims to identify the drivers of these aquatic N2O emissions using high-frequency in-situ sensor monitoring, providing the scientific basis for modelling the emissions at regional scale and for evaluating mitigation strategies.

Drainage mitigation measures. Measures that intercept nutrients in agricultural drainage water before it reaches streams, such as surface flow and subsurface flow constructed wetlands, integrated buffer zones, saturated buffer zones and controlled drainage, are a key part of Danish water management. They can remove substantial amounts of nitrogen, but some may also release phosphorus and emit greenhouse gases such as N2O and methane. You will synthesise results on greenhouse gas emissions and nitrogen and phosphorus retention from Danish drainage mitigation measures to give an overall assessment of their environmental performance and trade-offs.

Your main tasks will be to:

• carry out fieldwork, including sensor deployment and water and gas sampling

• process and analyse high-frequency sensor data and monitoring data

• compile and synthesise existing data on greenhouse gas emissions and nitrogen and phosphorus retention in drainage mitigation measures

• write scientific papers for international peer-reviewed journals

Your profile

The successful candidate must hold a PhD degree in biogeochemistry, aquatic ecology, environmental science, hydrology or a related field, and have a valid driving licence, as the position involves fieldwork in Danish agricultural landscapes.

It is an advantage if you have:

• experience with measurements of greenhouse gases (e.g. N2O, CH4) in aquatic systems or soils

• knowledge of nitrogen and phosphorus cycling in agricultural catchments, wetlands or constructed wetlands

• experience with analysis of large or high-frequency datasets, e.g. in R or Python

• a documented record of publishing in international peer-reviewed journals

We are looking for a candidate who can work independently as well as in a team, and who has good written and spoken English.

Who we are

The Department of Ecoscience is engaged in research programs and advisory work covering the major biological sub-disciplines. We conduct innovative, advanced research in the areas of aquatic biology and ecology, Arctic environments and ecosystems, biodiversity, conservation biology, and wildlife management. The Department currently employs approximately 300 academic and technical staff, as well as many PhD students.

The section has developed and tested many of the mitigation measures used in Danish water management, including constructed wetlands for treating drainage water, and advises national and international authorities.

The department actively facilitates a healthy integration of work and personal life and aspires to recruit and maintain highly skilled individuals who prioritise curiosity and trust.

• an exciting interdisciplinary environment with many national, international and industrial collaborators

• a research climate encouraging lively, open and critical discussion within and across different fields of research

• a work environment with close working relationships, networking and social activities

• a workplace characterised by professionalism, equality and a healthy work-life balance.

Place of work and area of employment

The place of work is Department of Ecoscience, Aarhus University, C.F. Møllers Allé 3, 8000 Aarhus C, Denmark. Fieldwork will take place at sites in Denmark.

Contact information

The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee, and each applicant is given the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that concerns him/her self.

jobs.occupation: Student Worker | Talent Acquisition

• Conducting references

• Scheduling interviews

jobs.occupation: Chief Technology Officer
jobs.description:
Lead engineering at a profitable, funded proptech while the team is still small enough to shape.

• Want to set the technical direction for a growing team and still ship code yourself?

• How would you keep a small team shipping to production many times a day, with review and testing that catch problems before customers do, without every decision landing on your desk?

• Where would you draw the line between what an AI agent should suggest and what it can do on a property owner’s behalf?

Sounds like you? Then you might be our next CTO!

A property owner with a portfolio of buildings has a practical question: which repairs belong in next year’s budget, and which can wait? At Proprty.ai, our models estimate the condition and remaining life of building components and the energy and CO2 effect of improving them. Our software turns those estimates into maintenance plans, and our AI agent, Tily, helps owners analyze their portfolios and take action!

Our product went live in 2024 and is used by customers in Denmark, Norway and Germany. We reached profitability by the end of 2025 and raised DKK 21 million in April 2026, and we are not planning to stop there!

There is still so much we can do to make it even better, and you could help shape the future of building maintenance and how engineering is run at Proprty.ai.

Product: TypeScript, React, and Next.js on Vercel, with Supabase (PostgreSQL, row-level security, storage).**

Data and models: Python and PySpark on Databricks (Azure, EU), Python model services, and LLM features on Azure OpenAI. We also run a customer API and an MCP server.

What you get to shape

The team and the code.

You'll lead our product engineering team, work closely with our data engineers and our Chief Data Science Officer, and keep building core features yourself. You might coach a developer through a tricky problem in the morning and ship a feature yourself that afternoon. You'll own engineering hiring as the team grows, from deciding which roles we need to choosing the people you want on the team.

How we build and ship.

You’ll own the platform’s architecture and how we test and release. We release to production many times a day. Your job is to keep that pace while making every release reliable and secure. When an urgent customer request competes with longer-term platform work, you’ll make the call and explain what comes first and why.

Shape what Tily can do next.

Our data scientists build models for building condition, remaining life, cost, and energy across several European markets. Together with our Chief Data Science Officer, you'll get those models in front of customers, decide what Tily may do on an owner's behalf, and use feedback from property owners, Sales, and Customer Success to choose the next problems to solve.

Change how we use AI ourselves.

Change how we use AI ourselves. Our engineers build with Claude Code and Cursor, AI agents review every pull request in our CI/CD pipeline, and agents take on routine work end to end so the team can ship faster. We keep looking for new ways AI can raise our pace, and you'll lead that.

We talk a lot (in a good way). When a problem gets tricky, we pull up a chair and pair on it. We like having a laugh while we figure things out.

What you’ll bring?

You've been CTO or head of engineering at a startup or scale-up while the product, the team, and the rules were still taking shape, and you can show what changed because you were there. You know when to open a pull request yourself, when to let another engineer make the call, and which shortcut will come back to bite you two releases from now.

You bring curiosity about our industry, our customers' problems, and the business acumen to understand how our product delivers business value, so that you can help facilitate features that drive outcomes and make our users' lives easier.

We’re AI-first (the name’s a bit of a giveaway). If you’ve built an agent or shipped an AI feature, we’d love to hear what happened after the demo. What did customers trust it to do, and where did they want the controls back? You’ll get to make those calls with Tily and figure out where AI helps our own engineers ship better software.

The core of what we consider for a candidate

• You’ve led an engineering team, coached developers, and hired people to join it.

• You’re keen to build AI agents that customers can put to work and to explore where AI makes your own team more effective.

• You still build full-stack features with React, TypeScript, and SQL. You can take a feature from technical design through thoughtful user experience to release, and measure what happens when customers get their hands on it.

• Fluent in English

Experience we’d love to hear about

• Taking an engineering team from a startup to a scale-up phase, understanding how and when to mature processes as the team scales, and how that looks different in this new AI era.

• Shipping an AI agent or feature into production. We’re especially curious about what you changed after people started using it.

• How you’ve spoken with customers and industry experts to help ensure we’re on the forefront of solving the right problems in our platform

• Your perspective on the role of a CTO as a thought leader.

• Working with PostgreSQL or Next.js, or building products for real estate or proptech.

Where we work

We spend 4 days a week together in our office near Rådhuspladsen. You’ll need to be based in the Copenhagen area, as we can’t offer relocation or visa sponsorship for this role.

New to proptech? That’s fine. If you’ve led engineers and still enjoy being one, we’d love to hear from you.

Questions? Reach out to Casper Høgh at Csh@ing.dk, who helps us land the right human for the job

Our hiring process

• 
Intro call with Casper Høgh – We’ll talk about your background, what you want from your next CTO role, and any questions you have about proprty.ai.

• 
In-person interview – Meet us at our Copenhagen office for a small demo and talk through the team, the decisions you’d own, and how you like to lead while staying hands-on.

• 
Case interview – Work through an engineering scenario with us. We want to understand what you’d prioritize, which trade-offs you see, and why.

• 
Board interview - Meet with one of our board members. Get their perspective on our journey and talk them through how you would help us in our next phase of growth.

• 
Offer – If we both see a fit, we’ll talk through the offer and next steps together.

TL;DR

Want to get in early with a great team? Love leading engineers and still writing code?

Apply now to lead our dev team and make building maintenance smarter and more sustainable with AI.

jobs.occupation: Marie Curie (MSCA) PhD scholarship in solar-driven hybrid methane production technologies for bio-electrochemical CO2 utilization - DTU Sustain
jobs.description:
If you are eager to advance sustainable solar-driven hybrid methane production technologies for bio-electrochemical CO2 utilization and contribute to solving one of the world’s most pressing environmental challenges, this position is for you.

At DTU Sustain, you will work at the forefront of environmental engineering and photo-bio-electrochemical technology, developing innovative solutions for CO2 utilization and methane production. You will gain hands-on experience with advanced analytical tools, reactor design, and reaction kinetics, skills that will prepare you for a future career in academia, research, or the biotechnology industry.

Responsibilities and qualifications
Your overall focus will be to advance the development of a sustainable photo-electrochemical process for methanation using biogenic CO2. You will work in close collaboration with an interdisciplinary research team in Water Technology and Processes section at DTU Sustain, combining environmental engineering, biotechnology, electrochemistry and process optimization to achieve more efficient CO2-to-CH4 conversion. The PhD position is funded by MSCA Doctoral Networks program.

Your primary tasks will be to:

• Cultivation of methanogenic archea
• Coupling electrochemical biofilm to photocathodes
• Design and conduct laboratory-scale photo-bio-electrochemical experiments
• Direct interspecies electron transfer mechanism characterization
• Optimize operating parameters to enhance process performance and robustness
• Analyze samples using advanced chemical and spectroscopic techniques (e.g., LC-MS, IC, TOC)
• Disseminate findings through scientific publications and conference presentations
We are looking for a candidate who has a strong experimental background in environmental biotechnology, electrochemistry, or chemical reaction engineering. Experience with analytical chemistry techniques for metabolite detecting and quantification is essential. A good command of both written and spoken English is required, along with the ability to work independently and as part of a collaborative, interdisciplinary research team.

You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

Assessment
The assessment of the applicants will be made by Professor Yifeng Zhang and the project team based on qualifications, relevant experience, and motivation for the project.

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. The allowance will be agreed upon with the relevant union. The period of employment is 3 years.

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information
Further information may be obtained from Prof. Yifeng Zhang (yifz@dtu.dk) 

https://orbit.dtu.dk/en/persons/yifeng-zhang

You can read more about DTU Sustain at www. https://sustain.dtu.dk/ 

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 15 February 2027 (23:59 Danish time).

Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae 
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
• 1-2 recommendation letters from experts in the field
You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it.

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

DTU Sustain - Department of Environmental and Resource Engineering - is one of the largest university departments specializing in environmental and resource engineering in Europe. The department conducts research, development & scientific advice and provides educational programs and service to society. We are working to develop new environmentally friendly and sustainable technologies, methods and solutions, and to disseminate this knowledge to society and future generations of engineers. The Department has approximately 300 staff from more than 30 nationalities.

Water Technology and Processes (WTP) Section
WTP focuses on greener and circular solutions for managing water and residual resources across urban, industrial, and agricultural settings. Research covers the full water continuum, from source water to wastewater, and includes micropollutant removal, advanced materials and membranes, environmental biotechnology, and holistic assessment of water technologies.

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.
